findings.title: Empty post-steer question bypasses continuation recovery

location.exact_code: raise RuntimeError("phase requested input without a question")

findings.basis: A post-steer guard failure with a native session must produce a durable usable continuation token and saved question.
findings.demonstrated_source_property: The needs-input question guard raises ordinary RuntimeError before the steered-specific guards; run_and_checkpoint catches only the special continuation exception.
findings.behavioral_consequence_unexecuted: A schema-valid needs-input receipt with question=null (or empty string) after an acknowledged budget steer becomes a generic failure receipt with no continuation checkpoint on a fresh run.
findings.minimal_repair: When steered, classify this semantic question guard as the candidate continuation exception; retain ordinary errors when unsteered.

steps: Build a fake native driver with canonical root identity and valid turn identity. Return TimeoutError twice, the valid steer acknowledgment, then turn/completed for that turn.
Its final JSON contains every schema field, matching phase, state="needs-input", summary="Obligations remain unverified.", question=None, and null unused fields.
Call run_and_checkpoint against a temporary Git repo with isolated BONAPARTE_HOME.
counterexample.expected_after_repair: A failed receipt <=4096 bytes carries a token; reading its checkpoint finds the continuation question; resume invokes thread/resume with the same root identity.

findings.title: Interrupted terminal is never made resumable
findings.basis: A soft time-budget interruption after a native session exists must return a usable continuation token.
findings.demonstrated_source_property: Every non-completed terminal status still raises RuntimeError; the wrapper catches only SoftBudgetInterruption.
findings.behavioral_consequence_unexecuted: The ordinary budget-expiry -> acknowledged steer -> interrupted terminal sequence loses its native-session continuation receipt.
findings.minimal_repair: For an interrupted terminal after steering, raise SoftBudgetInterruption; preserve non-budget ordinary errors.

steps: Use the visible fake-driver pattern with TimeoutError twice, a correlated successful steer result, and turn/completed {id: current_turn, status: "interrupted"}.
Call run_and_checkpoint on a temporary Git repo; then run main with that fake if checking the public failure receipt.
counterexample.expected_after_repair: The receipt is failed with a durable root-session token and continuation question; the next resume uses thread/resume for that session.

findings.title: Wrong steer turn identity is converted to a continuation checkpoint

location.exact_code: raise SoftBudgetInterruption("Codex app-server returned an invalid steer result")

findings.basis: Ordinary protocol errors must not create misleading continuation checkpoints.
findings.demonstrated_source_property: A steer response with result.turnId different from the active turn raises the recovery exception, which run_and_checkpoint unconditionally handles as resumable.
findings.behavioral_consequence_unexecuted: The implementation publishes a continuation checkpoint for a response-correlation/protocol failure even though it cannot establish that the budget steering targeted the active turn.
findings.minimal_repair: Keep invalid/corrupt steer results as RuntimeError; reserve the recovery exception for an identified interruption or post-steer semantic guard.

steps: After the fake driver expires the budget, return {id: steer_request_id, result: {turnId: "different-turn"}}.
Call run_and_checkpoint with canonical root identity and inspect the isolated checkpoint directory.
counterexample.expected_after_repair: A protocol failure has no newly created checkpoint or resume_token.

findings.title: Observer events can replace the root session used for recovery
findings.basis: Resuming the token must reuse the same native coordinator session.
findings.demonstrated_source_property: The continuation helper derives identity solely from observer.session_id. EventObserver.feed overwrites this field for every thread.started event, including native child threads; the exception stores no trusted root identity.
findings.behavioral_consequence_unexecuted: On a fresh run, an in-flight child thread.started notification can replace root R with child C. A later post-steer root guard failure saves token C, so resume continues the child rather than R.
findings.minimal_repair: Carry the validated root session in the special exception or restore observation.session_id from the validated thread/start identity before recovery (as C028 does).

steps: Fake thread/start returns canonical R and turn/start returns T.
Deliver thread/started for canonical child C while the phase is active, then budget expiry and valid steer acknowledgment, then a guarded root item/started for R followed by completion.
Inspect the failure receipt token and the threadId on a subsequent resume.
counterexample.expected_after_repair: The token and resume threadId equal R, never child C.

findings.evidence_kind: static source inspection; behavior derived, not executed

findings.title: Resumed guard failures retain stale Git identity
findings.basis: The continuation token returned after a post-steer guard failure must remain usable.
findings.demonstrated_source_property: The resume recovery branch delegates to _checkpoint_failure, whose _refresh_checkpoint_git(checkpoint) updates file inventories but defaults update_identity=False. Unlike the normal needs-input path, it does not refresh branch/identity_head.
findings.behavioral_consequence_unexecuted: If a resumed turn checks out its authorized branch or changes a detached commit before interruption, the saved branch/head remains stale; the next resume rejects the same worktree before sending thread/resume.
findings.minimal_repair: After the trusted same-session guard failure, refresh current Git identity with update_identity=True, require_identity=True, then persist the continuation question; handle refresh failures durably.

steps: Save a waiting-input checkpoint in a temporary Git repo on branch a.
Fake the resumed native turn to switch to branch b (or detach to another existing commit), then emit a budget interruption/post-steer guard failure.
Read the persisted checkpoint and call resume_checkpoint with Continue again, counting driver requests.
counterexample.expected_after_repair: The saved identity reflects the changed worktree; thread/resume uses the original checkpoint token instead of failing "different branch" or "different detached commit".

findings.title: Post-steer work guard does not correlate the item to the active turn
findings.origin: inherited baseline guard; newly material to candidate recovery behavior

location.exact_code: if isinstance(params, dict) and params.get("threadId") == session_id:

findings.basis: Guard decisions must identify the current turn; old-turn notifications should not fail a different turn or create a spurious recovery checkpoint.
findings.demonstrated_source_property: The detector checks only threadId before marking command/tool/file work after acknowledgment; turnId is not checked, although turn/start established a specific turn_id.
findings.behavioral_consequence_unexecuted: A queued item/started from an earlier turn on the same resumed thread is treated as forbidden current-turn work, causing a false failed receipt and continuation checkpoint.
findings.minimal_repair: Require params.get("turnId") == turn_id alongside threadId before setting post_steer_work.

steps: After a correlated successful budget steer acknowledgment for active turn T, feed item/started with threadId=R, turnId="old-turn", type="commandExecution".
Then complete T with a schema-valid needs-input wrap-up receipt containing the exact continuation question and an unverified summary.
Repeat with item turnId=T as the positive control.
counterexample.expected_after_repair: The old-turn event does not fail the phase; the current-turn event still triggers a continuation failure.

findings.title: Interrupted resumed turn keeps the consumed clarification and old question
findings.basis: A known post-steer continuation boundary should save the next continuation question and clear an answer that was already delivered; pending answers are for ambiguous at-least-once replay.
findings.demonstrated_source_property: The resume continuation catch only updates observations and calls _checkpoint_failure; it never replaces question or clears pending_answer.
findings.behavioral_consequence_unexecuted: After answering an ordinary clarification and hitting a guard failure, the failure receipt still asks the old question. Resuming with Continue is rejected as a different pending answer, and resuming without an answer replays the consumed clarification.
findings.minimal_repair: In the continuation catch set question=SOFT_BUDGET_CONTINUE_QUESTION and pending_answer=None before saving, while leaving generic transport failures on the replay path.
